{{Quote|We applaud the spirit of openness that this coalition embodies. As other worlds turn their back on the problem, these planets have instead embraced the people of the Republic with open arms.|[[Kaysil Verwood]], on Durkteel's membership in the Refugee Relief Movement|<ref name="HNN MRW">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|52|regional/13418_1.html|Mid Rim Worlds Open Ports to Refugees}}.</ref>}}
The '''Saurin''' were a [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]] who hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Durkteel/Legends|Durkteel]], in the [[Kastolar sector/Legends|Kastolar sector]] of the [[Kashyyyk Region/Legends|Kashyyyk Region]]. [[Reptile/Legends|Reptilian]] like the mainline Trandoshans of [[Trandosha/Legends|Trandosha]], the Saurin shared knobby, scaly skin; broad, flat noses; wide, gaping mouths; and sharp, jagged teeth with their cousins. In contrast, however, the Saurin had five-fingered hands instead of the Trandoshans' three digits (plus opposable thumb).

Durkteel was a member of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and a supporter of the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]]. Saurin [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] made their way to many worlds, and members of the species found work as thugs, combat trainers, bodyguards, and droid merchants. Other Saurin joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] in its [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|war]] with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Biology and appearance==
The Saurin or Saurins<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> were a [[Subspecies/Legends|subspecies]] of the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshans]]<ref name="ItWoSWT " /> and, as such, were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]]<ref name="SWC " /> [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]].<ref name="CSWE III 128" /> They had much in common with both their cousins and with other reptilian species, such as the [[Barabel/Legends|Barabels]]. Saurin had scaly skin that came of shades of brown,<ref name="SWC " /> green, purple,<ref name="M2-" /> and yellow.<ref name="SWC " /> Five-fingered hands were the primary feature to set them apart from mainline Trandoshans; some Saurin had human-like hands,<ref name="ItWoSWT " /><ref name="SWC " /> while others had clawed, reptilian hands like those of a Trandoshan.<ref name="SW2">[[Star Wars (2013) 2|''Star Wars'' (2013) 2]]</ref> The typical Saurin had scaly, three-toed feet. They ranged in build from fairly short and thin<ref name="TLC">''[[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]]''.</ref> to tall and muscular.<ref name="SW11">[[Star Wars (2013) 11|''Star Wars'' (2013) 11]]</ref> The subspecies was divided into two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]].<ref name="SWC " />

The typical Saurin had an elongated skull characterized by three spiky crests running down its length, one in the center and two on the sides. Smaller knobby patterns covered other portions of the head. Thick, bony ridges surrounded their dark, bulbous eyes. The snout sported a flat, stubby nose with two cavernous nostrils above a broad, gaping pink mouth brimming with sharp teeth.<ref name="TLC" /> Their features were flexible, allowing a Saurin to smile and express emotion.<ref name="SW15">[[Star Wars (2013) 15|''Star Wars'' (2013) 15]]</ref>

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|&hellip;This is Rus Kal Kin from Durkteel. Famous on his world for piloting refugee relief transports during the Separatist Crisis.|[[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="SW2" />}}
Saurin were not known for their senses of humor. Nevertheless, the most stoic members of the species could be amused by a joke from a gifted humorist like the [[Bimm/Legends|Bimm]] smuggler [[Rycar Ryjerd/Legends|Rycar Ryjerd]].<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref> Saurin names were composed of three elements: a first name, such as Gauron, Hrchek, or Sai'torr, and a two-word surname, such as Kal Fas and Nas Tal.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''.</ref>

Members of the species were capable of using standard-level technology, including the [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] and [[Transport/Legends|transports]],<ref name="SW2" /> and some Saurin became familiar with the technical specifications of such craft.<ref name="SW3">[[Star Wars (2013) 3|''Star Wars'' (2013) 3]]</ref> Saurin tended to wear clothing typical of other spacefaring cultures,<ref name="ANH" /><ref name="ROTJ" /><ref name="M2-" /> although some members of the subspecies chose to forego footwear.<ref name="TLC" />

==History==
[[File:Hrchek-kal-fas.jpg|left|thumb|[[Hrchek Kal Fas/Legends|Hrchek Kal Fas]] followed the droids [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] out of [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] but lost them in the streets of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].]]
The Saurin shared a common ancestry with other Trandoshans. Nevertheless, they split off from their mainline cousins at some point in their genetic history.<ref name="ItWoSWT " /> Physiological differences developed in the Saurin subspecies, included differently colored eyes and more digits on each hand.<ref name="ANH" />

The Saurin and mainline Trandoshans came to claim two different [[Planet/Legends|planets]] as their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworlds]]: [[Trandosha/Legends|Trandosha]], in the [[Kashyyyk system/Legends|Kashyyyk system]], for the standard Trandoshans, and [[Durkteel/Legends|Durkteel]] for the Saurin, a world situated a short distance from Trandosha along the [[Durkteel Loop/Legends|Durkteel Loop]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] in the neighboring [[Kastolar sector/Legends|Kastolar sector]]. Sometime between [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000]] and [[8000 BBY]], Durkteel became part of the greater [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] within the heavily explored region known as [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]].<ref name="EA" />

Durkteel eventually became a wealthy [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]], and investments included the construction of an ever-increasing number of orbiting [[Space station/Legends|space stations]]. Saurin pioneers joined [[Borneck]] and [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] counterparts in the colonization of [[Yitabo/Legends|Yitabo]], a world that lay at the junction of the Durkteel Loop and the [[Pabol Sleheyron/Legends|Pabol Sleheyron]]. Yitabo eventually became a minor agriworld in its own right. Investors swelled Saurin coffers with billions of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] in agribusiness, and over time the Saurin became one of the three most powerful indigenous groups in the greater [[Kashyyyk Region/Legends|Kashyyyk Region]], along with the Wookiees of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] and the [[Bimm (disambiguation)|Bimms]] of [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]].<ref name="EA" />

Durkteel did not avoid the influence of powerful neighbors beyond the region. By [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], their world and the hyperlanes that connected it with the otherside had fallen into the control of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], making Durkteel part of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="EA" /> This influence had been broken by [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], when the borders of Hutt Space retracted.<ref name="EA 129">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', 129.</ref> Shortly thereafter, however, the [[Jedi Civil War]] erupted, and by [[3959 BBY]], Durkteel had fallen into a region of space controlled by [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]] as part of his [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], a situation that persisted until [[3956 BBY]]. Hutt encroachment in the Kashyyyk Region brought Durkteel once more into the borders of Hutt Space by [[1004 BBY]], and again between [[52 BBY/Legends|52]] and [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="EA" />

Durkteel joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. With the eruption of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] that year, Durkteel sided with the Republic. The planet became a member of the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]], a group whose goal was to aid those fleeing conflict zones.<ref name="HNN MRW" /> The Saurin provided assistance to the relief movement in the form of skilled [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] who operated the [[Transport/Legends|transports]] carrying the refugees; at least one pilot, [[Rus Kal Kin]], gained fame on his homeworld for his transport-flying missions during the crisis.<ref name="SW2" /> Later that year, Durkteel joined nine other worlds to form the relief movement; members agreed to relax immigration laws and take in more refugees. Durkteel's population was 3.2 billion at this time.<ref name="HNN MRW" />

Nevertheless, Durkteel's proximity to Hutt Space once again placed its Saurin population in Hutt Space. As the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] erupted, the Saurin found their world in [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist Space]] as well. Hutt Space had once again retracted, leaving the Saurin outside its grasp, by [[4 BBY/Legends|4 BBY]]. By [[137 ABY]], however, Durkteel and its population fell within the region of space controlled by [[Darth Krayt]] as part of his [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="EA" />

==Saurin in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Spies? I'm no intelligence operative. I'm a pilot!|Rus Kal Kin upon being named a member of Stealth Squadron|<ref name="SW2" />}}
Saurin had spread beyond their homeworld as early as 32 BBY. That year, a Saurin thug was working for the criminal [[Green Hair]] as part of the [[Raptors (gang)|Raptors]] gang on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. When the group confronted the [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Darsha Assant]] and the information broker [[Lorn Pavan]], Assant used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to relieve the Saurin of his [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]], and Pavan stunned the gang member.<ref name="DMSH ">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> Another member of the species patronized the [[Seko Cantina]] on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] in [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]].<ref name="SWR21">[[Star Wars (1998) 21|''Star Wars'' (1998) 21]]</ref> Years later, a Saurin was among those plagued by [[Dianoga/Legends|dianogas]] in [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Desrini District]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="HNND">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|news/1359_3.html|Desrini Plagued by Dianogas}}.</ref> In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], a Saurin was gambling at a [[Casino/Legends|casino]] in [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] on the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] where [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] beat [[Barpotomous Drebble/Legends|Barpotomous Drebble]] in a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|Sabacc]].<ref name="LL">{{Tales|3|Lady Luck (comic story)}}.</ref>

[[File:Saitorr-kal-fas.jpg|thumb|right|[[Sai'torr Kal Fas/Legends|Sai'torr Kal Fas]] watched her cousin, Hrchek Kal Fas, as his personal bodyguard.]]
Two Saurin were at the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Cantina]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] came to charter passage off the world.<ref name="ANH" /> One of the Saurin was [[Hrchek Kal Fas/Legends|Hrchek Kal Fas]], a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] trader always on the lookout for cheap droids for sale, even if they were only available on the "invisible market."<ref name="Saurin CCG">{{CCG|set=A New Hope Limited|cardname=Saurin}}.</ref> Although he had come to the desert planet to investigate a possible business relationship with Tatooine's [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]],<ref name="FF CAN4">{{FactFile|22|CAN 1-6|Mos Eisley Cantina Characters}}.</ref> he heard news of a reward for two stolen droids, supposedly "close companions" of an Imperial officer. He saw through this cover story, but when he witnessed [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] wander into the cantina, he suspected they might be the droids in question. He tailed them out into the streets of Mos Eisley, but they were nowhere to be seen.<ref name="CSWE II 195">{{CSWECite|II|195}}</ref> The droid trader hired the tall [[Ranat/Legends|Ranat]]'' [[Nevar Yalnal/Legends|Nevar Yalnal]]'' to do unskilled labor for him.<ref name="NY CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Nevar Yalnal}}.</ref> Hrchek Kal Fas also retained the services of his cousin, Sai'torr Kal Fas.<ref name="SWE ">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref><ref name="CVD ">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> She was a savvy warrior and combat instructor who took on students she deemed to have the right potential.<ref name="SKF CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Sai'torr Kal Fas}}.</ref>

Also in 0 BBY, a Saurin was present in the streets of Mos Eisley as the spy [[Garindan/Legends|Garindan]] shadowed Luke Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi on their way to [[Docking Bay 94/Legends|Docking Bay 94]].<ref name="ANH" /> Later that year, a Saurin was captured on holofilm in the streets of Mos Eisley and broadcast as part of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] program "[[Life on Tatooine]]."<ref name="SWHS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''.</ref>

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Rebellion]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] against the rule of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the famed transport pilot Rus Kal Kin proved himself as an [[Ace/Legends|ace]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] pilot<ref name="SW2" /> and a trusted member of the Alliance.<ref name="SW3" /> Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Saurin was hand-picked by the [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] to serve in a top-secret [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]], its mission to clandestinely seek out a new base of operations for the Alliance while simultaneously rooting out an Imperial [[Spy/Legends|spy]].<ref name="SW2" /> Rus Kal Kin flew several missions with this [[Stealth Squadron]],<ref name="SW4">[[Star Wars (2013) 4|''Star Wars'' (2013) 4]]</ref><ref name="SW11" /> and once its mission had been completed, he stayed on as an inaugural member of the squadron's successor, [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]].<ref name="SW15" />

Combat trainer [[Gauron Nas Tal/Legends|Gauron Nas Tal]] also plied his trade on Tatooine. He worked for [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] as a combat instructor for the gangster's [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] guards. The Saurin came to hate both his employment and his employer, and by [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], he was plotting to kill the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]].<ref name="GNT CCG">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Garon Nas Tal}}.</ref> When the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and one of Nas Tal's Gamorrean trainees fell into Jabba's [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] pit, the Saurin joined the other members of the Hutt's entourage in watching the battle below. The Gamorrean stood little chance against the rancor, although the [[Human/Legends|Human]] managed to kill the beast.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Gauron Nas Tal later accompanied Jabba on his sail barge the [[Khetanna/Legends|Khetanna]]. He died when the vessel exploded during the [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]].<ref name="I60-86">{{InsiderCite|60|Who's Who in Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Saurinmarvel.jpg|thumb|left|upright|A Saurin informs [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] bar fight in the Marvel Comics adaptation of ''A New Hope.'']]
The Saurin were one of the many alien species designed for the cantina sequence of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], released in [[1977]]. They were known as Crocs,<ref name="AFA ">''[[Star Wars: The Action Figure Archive]]''</ref> Crockers, and Gila-Men during production and principal photography in England. One of the two characters was supposed to be given the proper name Gilaass.<ref name="CRC 3">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> The [[Marvel Comics]] adaptation of the film shows a Saurin informing Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] of the presence of Obi-Wan Kenobi in the Mos Eisley Cantina, a task performed by the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Garouf Lafoe/Legends|Garouf Lafoe]] in the original film.<ref name="M2-" />

The production team of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] altered one of the Saurin masks from ''A New Hope'' for use for the Trandoshan [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]]. Modifications for the Bossk design included repainting the mask, changing the eyes, and creating new, less Humanlike arms and legs.<ref name="AFA " /> An unmodified Saurin mask was used for a member of Jabba the Hutt's entourage in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] in [[1983]].<ref name="BTM" />

In [[1995]], [[Decipher]] dubbed the species the Saurin as part of its ''[[Premiere Limited]]'' and ''[[A New Hope Limited]]'' sets of cards for the ''[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]''.<ref name="CRC 3" /> The company also named the Saurin characters seen in the films and gave them simple backstories. The cards have game effects related to the characters' personalities and skills. For example, the Sai'torr Kal Fas card can be used to "train" and improve the combat skills of another character,<ref name="SKF CCG" /> while the Gauron Nas Tal (here spelled "Garon Nas Tal") card increases the power of any Saurin characters that have already been improved by Sai'torr Kal Fas.<ref name="GNT CCG" /> The article "[[50 Factoids About the Original Star Wars Trilogy|50 Factoids about the Original Star Wars Trilogy]]" mistakenly says that a Saurin character was added to the cantina scene of the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] of ''A New Hope'';<ref name="50F ">{{InsiderCite|78|50 Factoids About the Original Star Wars Trilogy|50 Factoids About the Original ''Star Wars'' Trilogy}}</ref> the character in question is actually a [[Sarkan/Legends|Sarkan]], a different reptilian species.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|melas|Melas}}.</ref>

[[File:Hrchek_Kal_Fas_action_figure.jpg|thumb|right|upright|The Hrchek Kal Fas action figure from [[Hasbro]] features more reptilian hands and feet than the Saurin who appear in ''A New Hope.'']]
The species has since played little role in ''Star Wars'' fiction, and their society, culture, and history remain largely unexplored. ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]'' is one exception and reveals that Saurin are a Trandoshan subspecies,<ref name="ItWoSWT " /> and ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' is another, as it reveals some details about Durkteel and its economy.<ref name="EA" /> Nevertheless, their history remains sketchy and questions remain, such as whether they split from their Trandoshan cousins before or after they moved to Durkteel. Other Saurin have largely been background characters. For example, the ''A New Hope'' Saurin appear in the background of the [[A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale (webstrip)|''A Hunter's Fate: Greedo's Tale'' webstrip]], ''[[Star Wars Manga: A New Hope]]'', "[[The Emperor's Court]]," and the [[Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition|''Star Wars: A New Hope - The Special Edition'' comic book]]. In October [[2002]], artist [[Derek Thompson]] sketched a group of [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] as possible participants in the Clone Wars for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Among the characters, all representatives of species from the cantina sequence of ''A New Hope'', is one Saurin. In the end, [[George Lucas]] rejected the concept.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>

In [[2009]], [[Hasbro]] released an action figure of Hrchek Kal Fas as part of its [[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]] line of toys. The action figure differs from the on-screen depiction of the Saurin in that it wears no gloves, has more reptilian hands, and wears no boots. Hasbro calls this a "creative decision" taken to make the character seem more alien; they argue that had the Saurin featured more prominently in ''A New Hope,'' [[George Lucas]] would have given them more non-human characteristics.<ref>{{Rebelscum|url=story/front/Hasbros_77th_STAR_WARS_QA_The_Answers_126309.asp|text=Hasbro's 77th STAR WARS Q&A: The Answers!}}</ref> The Saurin action figure also features gold eyes with black pupils, another discrepancy from the original film. Hasbro blames this on a production error among the Chinese production staff; they ordered the toys corrected to have black eyes.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.collectionstation.com/groups/Star-Wars/Official-Hasbro-Star-Wars-Q-A-103_60|text=Official Hasbro Star Wars Q & A - 10/3|work=[https://web.archive.org/web/20090926193447/http://www.collectionstation.com CollectionStation.com]|archivedate=20091009010128|nolive=1}}</ref>
